title: Quantum Trading 101
subtitle: What quantum computers can — and can't yet — do for markets: the theory, working code, and an honest map of the field.
summary: “Quantum trading” means two different things: a serious research programme at banks and labs, and a marketing word used by scams. This course gives you just enough physics to reason for yourself, the three algorithm families that matter to finance, labs that run real simulations in your browser, and a dated, sourced map of who has demonstrated what. You finish by writing a Quantum Readiness Brief for a trading desk.
outcomes: Explain qubits, measurement and entanglement using your own simulations — and why classical computers struggle to simulate them.
Describe how amplitude estimation, optimisation (QAOA, annealing) and quantum machine learning target pricing, portfolios and prediction — and where each speed-up claim stops.
Price an option with Monte Carlo and compare it against ideal quantum amplitude estimation; formulate a portfolio as a QUBO and solve it three ways.
Read a “quantum advantage” headline critically: the claim, the evidence level, the counter-evidence.
Recognise the tells of “Quantum AI” trading scams.
Produce a sourced Quantum Readiness Brief for a trading desk, including post-quantum security.
prerequisites: Helpful, not required: what an option and a portfolio are (both are explained)
